elements_selected.content:
Replace the hardcoded include_str!() calls in engine.rs with a compile-time embedding mechanism that loads all themes from the themes/ directory.

Approach: Use the `include_dir` crate (or a build.rs that generates a static HashMap). The key decision is:

Option A — `include_dir` crate:
  Add `include_dir = "0.7"` to Cargo.toml. In engine.rs:
  ```rust
  use include_dir::{include_dir, Dir}
  static BUNDLED_THEMES: Dir = include_dir!("$CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/themes");
  ```
  Lookup: BUNDLED_THEMES.get_file(format!("{theme}/{template}"))

Option B — build.rs codegen:
  Generate a Rust source file that contains static &str constants for each theme/template pair. More control, no extra dependency.

Recommendation: Option A is simpler and well-maintained. Use it unless the dependency is unacceptable.

After this task, delete src/web/templates/ — themes/default/ is now the single source of truth for built-in templates. Update all references.

Create a helper function:
  fn bundled_template(theme: &str, name: &str) -> Option<&'static str>
that looks up a template from the embedded directory. Returns None if the theme or template does not exist.

Also create:
  fn bundled_theme_names() -> Vec<&'static str>
that returns the list of all embedded theme directory names.
